name: knowledge-worker
description: Turning work into documents other people can act on — repo documentation, walkthrough recordings, video and meeting intake, and handoffs that survive a context reset.
$note: The kit for someone whose output is understanding rather than code — a product owner, an analyst, a technical writer. It is the one kit that assumes the least about the target repo: none of these skills needs a build, a stack, or a deploy target.
$overlapNote: agent-notepad and handoff are also in agent-ops. That is deliberate and is NOT a 'one artifact, one home' violation: one home is about which repo OWNS the directory, and exactly one does. A kit only references a skill by name, so two kits naming it create no second copy and nothing that can drift. Kits are curated bundles; overlap between them is the normal case.
